about.description:
elkjs is a JavaScript transpilation of the Eclipse Layout Kernel (ELK), which provides
automatic layout algorithms for node-link diagrams — most notably the `layered`
algorithm for hierarchical graphs, with orthogonal edge routing.

It has no runtime dependencies. `elk.bundled.js` runs the layout in-process and is the
build to use where a Web Worker is not available.

name: elkjs
raw_meta_yaml:
context:
  version: "0.9.3"

package:
  name: elkjs
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://registry.npmjs.org/elkjs/-/elkjs-${{ version }}.tgz
  sha256: b95b224bd1ab71fd40f6d9a6365c28d989745dff6b0d514407bc1eb68f2f561e

build:
  number: 0
  noarch: generic

requirements:
  build:
    - nodejs

tests:
  # QuickJS rather than Node: the package is plain JavaScript with no dependencies and no runtime
  # of its own, and this is what demonstrates it.
  - script:
      - qjs -m test_elkjs.js
    requirements:
      run:
        - quickjs
    files:
      recipe:
        - test_elkjs.js

about:
  # The lib/ bundles carry code from elkjs's Java dependencies, via GWT, and from its
  # JavaScript bundler. The npm tarball only ships ELK's own licence, so the others come
  # from the recipe directory; THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md says which component is under which.
  license: EPL-2.0 AND EPL-1.0 AND Apache-2.0 AND Apache-1.1 AND MIT
  license_file:
    - LICENSE.md
    - LICENSE-EPL-1.0.txt
    - LICENSE-Apache-2.0.txt
    - LICENSE-Apache-1.1.txt
    - LICENSE-MIT-browser-pack.txt
    - LICENSE-MIT-umd.txt
    - LICENSE-MIT-babel.txt
    - THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md
  summary: JavaScript build of the Eclipse Layout Kernel, for laying out node-link diagrams
  description: |
    elkjs is a JavaScript transpilation of the Eclipse Layout Kernel (ELK), which provides
    automatic layout algorithms for node-link diagrams — most notably the `layered`
    algorithm for hierarchical graphs, with orthogonal edge routing.

    It has no runtime dependencies. `elk.bundled.js` runs the layout in-process and is the
    build to use where a Web Worker is not available.
  homepage: https://github.com/kieler/elkjs
  repository: https://github.com/kieler/elkjs
  documentation: https://eclipse.dev/elk/documentation.html

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - chrisburr
